adScenario.ausscherer_stauende: The vehicle ahead pulls out shortly before a standing vehicle; the ego has to react.
adScenario.autobahn_ausfahrt: The ego starts on the left lane, changes two lanes to the right in time and leaves the highway over the deceleration lane.
adScenario.autobahn_ueberholen: Three-lane highway: a slower vehicle on the right lane is overtaken on the left, then the ego returns to the right lane (keep-right rule).
adScenario.einfaedeln_lkw: Highway entry after Werling 5.3.2: merging from the acceleration lane into the gap between two trucks.
adScenario.einscherer: A slower vehicle cuts in from the left 22 m ahead of the ego.
adScenario.innerorts_werling: Urban road after Werling 5.3.1 at 30 km/h: parked cars, two pedestrians step onto the road from between parked cars and are visible late, an oncoming vehicle turns left wrongly at the junction, two cyclists at the roadside.
adScenario.kreisverkehr: Single-lane roundabout: entry from the west, yielding to the traffic in the ring, exit to the east.
adScenario.kreuzung_ampel_geradeaus: The ego approaches at red, stops at the stop line and drives straight on at green; cross traffic drives during the ego's red phase.
adScenario.kreuzung_vorfahrt_links: The ego comes from the minor road, yields to the cross traffic and turns left.
adScenario.laengsparken_rueckwaerts: Reverse parallel parking into an 8.5 m gap: forward beside the gap, stop, change of direction at standstill, reverse to the middle of the gap.
adScenario.landstrasse_ueberholen: Country road with a slow truck and oncoming traffic: overtaking over the oncoming lane only with a sufficient gap; no overtaking in the section with a solid center line.
adScenario.notausweichen_hindernis: A broken-down vehicle becomes visible only 60 m ahead; evasion onto the free left lane.
adScenario.verkehrsdichte_20: Three-lane ring road with 20 vehicles per km and lane, IDM car following and MOBIL lane changes, 10 % trucks.
adScenario.werling_autobahnversuch: Highway experiment after Werling 5.3.2: merging between trucks, a delayed lane change because of a fast approaching car, a truck pulling out and a side-wind gust (lateral_impulse) at t = 38.5 s.

adScenarioLabel.ausscherer_stauende: Cut-out at the end of a queue

tracking_controller.composite: Combination of a lateral and a longitudinal controller

steering_powertrain.purpose: Connects the outputs of the trajectory controller with the plant.
steering_powertrain.summary: Integrates the steering rate or takes the steering angle, and models the steering actuator (latency, characteristic, rate limit) and delayed drive and brake torques.

rule_based.purpose: Behavior layer after Werling 3.6: choose the targets so that the reactive trajectory planning rarely has to avoid a collision.
rule_based.summary: State machine for lane keeping, lane changes, merging, overtaking, intersections, roundabouts and parking; it provides the reference curve, the longitudinal modes and the corridor for the trajectory planner.

ground_truth.purpose: Reference for developing prediction, behavior and planning without perception errors.
ground_truth.summary: Passes on the objects of the scenario engine and the true ego state unchanged.

object_sensor.purpose: More realistic inputs for prediction and behavior: limited range, occlusion, measurement noise, missed detections and latency; reproducible through the scenario seed.
object_sensor.summary: Creates a disturbed object list and an estimate of the ego state from the ground truth.

constant_acceleration.purpose: Prediction of leading and gap vehicles for the following and merging modes after Werling 3.5.2.
constant_acceleration.summary: Predicts objects with constant acceleration along their lane in Frenet coordinates.

constant_velocity.purpose: Simple reference prediction that needs no map, for example for pedestrians.
constant_velocity.summary: Straight-line prediction with constant speed (optionally constant yaw rate).

lane_following.purpose: Detects lane changes (cut-ins) early from the lateral speed relative to the lane.
lane_following.summary: Constant speed along the lane sequence; the lateral offset converges to the center of the target lane.

acc.purpose: Comparison of trajectory-based longitudinal control with a classical ACC without a planner.
acc.summary: Distance-based longitudinal control with a constant time gap.

composite.purpose: Classical decoupled lateral and longitudinal control as a comparison with the coupled Werling control.
composite.summary: Combines any lateral and any longitudinal controller into one tracking controller.

ff_fb.purpose: Time-based longitudinal tracking (trajectory instead of path).
ff_fb.summary: Acceleration feedforward from the trajectory with feedback of the speed and longitudinal errors.

lqr.summary: State feedback on the lateral error model of the single-track model with a discrete Riccati solution, gain scheduling over speed and a steady-state feedforward.

mpc.purpose: Comparison controller that takes actuator limits into account explicitly (Werling Tab. 4.1).
mpc.summary: Linear time-varying model predictive lateral control along the trajectory horizon with limits on steering angle and steering rate.

pi.summary: PI controller on the speed error.

pid.summary: PID controller on the speed error of the planned trajectory.

pure_pursuit.summary: Geometric lateral controller: a circular arc from the rear axle to a target point on the path.

speed_pi.purpose: Robust speed controller under actuator saturation.
speed_pi.summary: PI speed controller with back-calculation anti-windup and feedforward.

stanley.purpose: Comparison controller with good tracking at medium speeds.
stanley.summary: Lateral controller on the lateral error of the front axle and the heading error (Stanley, DARPA Grand Challenge).

werling_bilevel.purpose: Combines the low-level stabilization (permanent disturbances, model errors) with the high-level stabilization by re-initialization after impulse disturbances (Werling 2.3, 4.4, 4.5).
werling_bilevel.summary: Default tracking controller: bumpless switching between the three Werling controllers by reference point and driving direction, plus the trigger of re-initializations and the motion prediction for the planner.

werling_dynamic.purpose: Stabilizes a reference point ahead of the center of gravity on the planned trajectory; the speed-dependent look-ahead keeps the damping of the zero dynamics constant (Werling 4.3).
werling_dynamic.summary: Exactly input-output linearizing tracking controller on the dynamic single-track model with an isotropic Pacejka tire, for fast driving.

werling_kinematic_center.purpose: Stabilizes the point about half a wheelbase ahead of the rear axle directly, so the vehicle steers more calmly (Werling 4.2.4).
werling_kinematic_center.summary: Lyapunov-based tracking controller of the geometric vehicle center without orientation stabilization, for slow forward driving.

werling_kinematic_orientation.purpose: Stabilizes position, orientation, speed and steering angle of the extended kinematic single-track model along the trajectory, also at standstill and in reverse (Werling 4.2.3).
werling_kinematic_orientation.summary: Lyapunov-based tracking controller of the rear-axle center with orientation stabilization, for slow forward and reverse driving.

frenet_naive.purpose: Shows the benefit of temporal consistency (Werling Fig. 3.2) in planner comparisons.
frenet_naive.summary: Comparison planner: Frenet sampling with a relative end-time grid and replanning from the measured state.

learned.purpose: Learned planning with the safety of the Werling planner: if no local candidate is valid, or the best one lies on the border of the local set, the cycle searches completely.
learned.summary: A network proposes the trajectory (end offset, end speed, end times); the Werling planner builds only the candidates next to the proposal and checks them with its restrictions and collision check.

sequential.purpose: Shows the advantage of the combined lateral and longitudinal optimization (evasion with matched braking).
sequential.summary: Comparison planner: the longitudinal motion without knowledge of the lateral motion, then the lateral motion (Werling 3.1).

werling.purpose: Reactive, time-critical collision avoidance with combined longitudinal and lateral optimization, temporally consistent by Bellman's principle while no restriction is active (Werling 2011, ch. 3).
werling.summary: Trajectory planning after Werling: optimal polynomials in Frenet coordinates, discretized target manifolds on an absolute time grid, temporal consistency and bi-level stabilization.

werling_parking.purpose: Parking maneuvers with changes of direction, which the Frenet planner cannot represent on the reference line.
werling_parking.summary: Werling planner for normal driving; for a parking task a Hybrid A* / Reeds-Shepp planner plans the parking path and hands it to the controller one move at a time.

split_range.purpose: The design models of the tracking controllers neglect rolling and air resistance; this layer compensates them and removes remaining errors (head wind, slope) with an integrator.
split_range.summary: Converts the desired longitudinal force or acceleration into wheel torques through drive or brake.

vehicle_model.purpose: Any vehicle model (Werling design models, single-track, double-track, multibody) as the plant for controller development and robustness studies.
vehicle_model.summary: Wraps a registered vdsim vehicle model as the plant of the control chain.

scenario_engine.purpose: Reproducible test scenarios for the whole chain: actors with IDM/MOBIL, scripted triggers, traffic lights, collision and off-road detection, and disturbance events.
scenario_engine.summary: Simulates the road users of a scenario and provides the ground truth.

kpi.lateral_displacement: Lateral displacement 1.07 s after steering start
kpi.yaw_ratio_175s: Yaw rate 1.75 s after steering end
kpi.yaw_ratio_1s: Yaw rate 1.0 s after steering end

brake_in_turn.description: Steady-state circle, then braking with constant deceleration
brake_in_turn.label: Braking in a turn (ISO 7975)

circle.description: Constant-radius circle with slowly rising speed (understeer gradient)
circle.label: Steady-state circle (ISO 4138)

custom.description: Segment list as JSON: [["straight", L, v_kmh], ["arc", R, angle_deg, v_kmh], ...]
custom.label: Custom test cycle

emergency_evasion.description: Fast evasion around an obstacle and return to the lane
emergency_evasion.label: Emergency evasion

frequency_sweep.description: Steering sweep to identify the frequency response (ISO 7401)
frequency_sweep.label: Frequency response (sine sweep)

highway.description: Highway with clothoid curves and a lane change
highway.label: Highway

iso_double_lane_change.description: Double lane change through cone gates per ISO 3888-1 (offset 3.5 m)
iso_double_lane_change.label: ISO double lane change (ISO 3888-1)

lane_change.description: Single lane change with sinusoidal curvature (heading 0 at the end)
lane_change.label: Lane change

race_track.description: Circuit with a computed minimum-curvature line and GGV speed profile
race_track.label: Race track (racing line)

ramp_steer.description: Slowly increasing steering angle at constant speed
ramp_steer.label: Ramp steer (ISO 4138)

sine_with_dwell.description: ESC test: 0.7 Hz sine with 500 ms dwell
sine_with_dwell.label: Sine with dwell (FMVSS 126)

step_steer.description: Step steering input at constant speed
step_steer.label: Step steer (ISO 7401)

tires.combined_lateral_reduction: Combined slip: reduction of Fy by kappa (B_yk)
tires.combined_longitudinal_reduction: Combined slip: reduction of Fx by alpha (B_xa)
tires.cornering_stiffness_front: Cornering stiffness front (per tire, nominal load)
tires.cornering_stiffness_rear: Cornering stiffness rear (per tire, nominal load)
tires.load_sensitivity_stiffness: Load sensitivity of cornering stiffness (Pacejka p_Ky2)
